Description: UKPConvArg1: MTurk workers' pairwise judgements of which of two web arguments is more convincing, 16,927 pairs of 1,052 arguments in 32 debates. One row per vote; 'equal' = draw; rater = worker.
Reference: Habernal, I., & Gurevych, I. (2016). Which argument is more convincing? Analyzing and predicting convincingness of Web arguments using bidirectional LSTM. Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), 1589-1599.
Notes: Full corpus (UKPConvArg1-full-XML), commit ca9d24e. Worker ids re-keyed; argument texts and free-text reasons not included. Built by data/competitions/ukpconvarg1.R.

Description: University Challenge (BBC) main-series match results, 1994-95 to 2026-27 (in progress), parsed from the Wikipedia series pages. One row per match with scores, series and stage.
Reference: Wikipedia contributors. University Challenge series pages 1994-95 to 2026-27. English Wikipedia (revisions of 2026-10-01).
Notes: Share-alike. Christmas specials excluded. Institutions keyed by Wikipedia article (redirects resolved). Built by data/competitions/university_challenge.R.

Description: Wild vervet monkey dyadic aggressive interactions, 66 animals, 2015-2017. One row per interaction with native draws and undecided outcomes.
Reference: Vilette, C., Bonnell, T., Henzi, P., & Barrett, L. (2020). Comparing dominance hierarchy methods using a data-splitting approach with real-world data. Behavioral Ecology, 31(6), 1379-1390.
Notes: agent_a = aggressor. winner 'draw' covers draws (result 3) and undecided (result 4); see result. The deposit's GPL-3 file covers its R package code only. Built by data/competitions/vervets.R.

Description: Retrosheet MLB game logs, 1871-2025: every major-league regular-season game (NA, NL, AA, UA, PL, AL, FL) plus wildcard, division, LCS and World Series games. One row per game; agent_a = home team, with scores, park, attendance, doubleheader number, forfeit and protest codes.
Reference: Retrosheet. Game logs, 1871-2025 (gl1871_2025.zip, downloaded 2026-10-01). https://www.retrosheet.org
Custom License (source): Retrosheet notice (www.retrosheet.org/notice.txt): free to make any desired use of the information, including selling it or giving it away, provided the credit statement appears prominently.
Custom License (derived): The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at www.retrosheet.org.
Notes: Ruled permissive custom licence in #2702. All-Star games dropped. Forfeits: winner follows the forfeit code (V/H); T (no-decision) = draw. Overlaps the existing comps table mlb_through2023 (538-based); this one adds pre-538 leagues, postseason flags, parks and attendance. Retrosheet event files (plate appearances, pitches) not included; possible follow-up. Built by data/competitions/retrosheet_mlb.R.

Description: pklmart doubles pickleball game results, 2021-2025: 928 games between 789 two-player teams, skill levels 2.5 to Pro, entered by players through the pklmart data-entry tool. One row per game; agent_a = winning team; scores, match, skill level and scoring format kept.
Reference: pklmart (2025). pklmart's Competitive Pickleball Extracts (version 6). Kaggle. https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/cakesofspan/pklmarts-competitive-pickleball-extracts
Notes: Non-commercial share-alike (#2714). Kaggle version 6 (2025-04-20). Agents are player-id pairs; 6 level-score (unfinished) games and 1 game with an unknown team dropped; rallies and shots not included. Built by data/competitions/pklmart_pickleball.R.

Description: Clark et al. (2018) Study 2: raters chose which of two photos of men looked physically stronger. 7,835 decisions on 82 photos by 96 raters; agent_a = photo chosen. Study 1 is already in IRW as elochoice_physical.
Reference: Clark, A. P., Howard, K. L., Woods, A. T., Penton-Voak, I. S., & Neumann, C. (2018). Why rate when you could compare? Using the 'EloChoice' package to assess pairwise comparisons of perceived physical strength. PLOS ONE, 13(1), e0190393.
Notes: EloStrengthData.zip Study2Pairwise.csv; 22 rows pairing a photo with itself dropped. rater_age/rater_sex from the source. One of the openly licensed studies in the Kinnear, Jones & Davies CJ meta-analysis. Script data/competitions/kinnear_cj_open.R (#2692).

Description: Mathematicians' comparative judgements of which of two proofs is more explanatory: 9 proofs, 38 judges, 760 decisions in two groups (Auckland, Rutgers); agent_a = proof chosen.
Reference: Mejía Ramos, J. P., Evans, T., Rittberg, C., & Inglis, M. (2021). Mathematicians' assessments of the explanatory value of proofs. Axiomathes, 31(5), 575-599.
Notes: NonCommercial. Decisions-combined.csv; candidate codes mapped to proof names via ModelledRes.csv; judges re-keyed. Script data/competitions/kinnear_cj_open.R (#2692).

Description: Undergraduates' comparative judgements of 15 proofs of the same theorem on one criterion per session (rigour, insight, simplicity, understanding, marks; 7 sessions in two studies): 3,969 decisions by 227 judges; agent_a = proof chosen.
Reference: Sangwin, C., & Kinnear, G. (2021). Investigating insight and rigour as separate constructs in mathematical proof. EdArXiv.
Notes: Zenodo licence 'Other (Open)'; the archived repository's LICENSE.md is the MIT License (George Kinnear, 2021). judgement_data_all.csv; script ids mapped to proof numbers so agents are shared across sessions; excluded = 1 for the judges the authors dropped (median time < 5 s). Script data/competitions/kinnear_cj_open.R (#2692).

Description: Protect our Planet from Solar Storms (Zooniverse): citizen scientists chose which of two coronal mass ejection images looked more complicated. 409,889 decisions on 1,111 images by 5,898 raters in two sessions (original 2018; brightness-equalised 2019-20); agent_a = image chosen.
Reference: Jones, S. R., Scott, C. J., Barnard, L. A., Highfield, R., Lintott, C. J., & Baeten, E. (2020). The visual complexity of coronal mass ejections follows the solar cycle. Space Weather, 18(10), e2020SW002556.
Notes: Zooniverse classification exports (classifications_complete, classifications_brightness_equalised); user names, ids and IP hashes dropped, raters re-keyed; not-logged-in raters are per browser session (rater_logged_in = 0). Script data/competitions/kinnear_cj_open.R (#2692).

Description: SSCAIT (Student StarCraft AI Tournament & Ladder) bot ladder: 115,183 one-on-one StarCraft: Brood War games among 110 bots, 2021-03 to 2024-01. One row per game; every game has a winner (crash = loss; time-limit games decided on score, flagged timelimit).
Reference: Čertický, M., Churchill, D., Kim, K.-J., Čertický, M., & Kelly, R. (2018). StarCraft AI competitions, bots, and tournament manager software. IEEE Transactions on Games, 11(3), 227-237.
Notes: Non-commercial (ruled 10-01, #2681). All games the API serves (pages of 1,000, fetched 2026-10-01); the ladder stopped playing after the site changed host. agent_a = host, agent_b = guest. Built by data/competitions/sscait_ladder.R.

Description: Men's international rugby union test matches between the ten tier-one nations (Argentina, Australia, England, France, Ireland, Italy, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa, Wales), 1871-2026, parsed from the 45 Wikipedia head-to-head pages. One row per test with scores, venue and competition; agent_a = home side, homefield blank at neutral venues.
Reference: Wikipedia contributors. History of rugby union matches between [nation] and [nation], 45 pages. English Wikipedia (revisions current on 2026-10-01).
Notes: Share-alike. Built from Wikipedia's own tables, not the Kaggle relabel (#2708). Uncapped XV and non-test matches excluded; 58 goal-era scores kept as text in score_raw. Revision ids pinned in the script. Built by data/competitions/rugby_union_tier1.R.
